record.title: The Cellar Door
record.premise: On their own account, the Toh-Wo gets into Fort Chalkmoth's keep by the wall captain's price or by the trapdoor in the yard, finds jars of Jal-Veesa's sap stacked by the stair in the quartermaster's store, faces the order's gaoler in the guardroom, and finds the cellar's inner door locked with moaning behind it and its key not in the fort.
record.foundation: Built from the main plot (§5 quest 12, passed by the owner). The player's own errand, begun by the wounded scout's words and Never-Writes-Twice's answer in MN11; it runs beside MN13 (the hunt) and either may come first. Four steps in the plot's order where it gives one: the way in (the captain's price, or the trapdoor in the yard unseen), then the store, the gaoler and the door, which the player may do in any order once inside, as one working stage (quest-write §3.4) with three objectives. The fort's main source, Fort Neugrad, gives the keep (its Adept lock serves as the store's door) and the prison below it (the cellar), whose passage door is set as the trapdoor in the yard and comes up into the guardroom. The gaoler's test is the "spell cast in front of a person as a test" block (owner, #73), to be proven once; until proven the gate stands in as Illusion 25. The plot has two people speak first (the wall captain at the gate and the gaoler); the ceiling allows one, so the gaoler speaks first (every way in meets him) and the captain stands at the gate with a marker and the objective. The cellar's question stays open: the player learns only that sap from Jal-Veesa is stored by the stair in a fort with no Hist, the gaoler's "they sleep, and they dream", and moaning behind a door whose key is not in the fort. The last stage turns the player back to the hunt: to Bell Station if MN13 is not yet done, to the seal-stones if it is.

truth.what: The Toh-Reel-Ka keep dreamers locked in the old Legion prison below the keep, feed them sap and have them tell their dreams; Never-Writes-Twice ran the cellar and keeps the inner door's only key away from the fort (argonia-4e201-state §2.5, §11.2; plot §3).

Jars of Hist sap come up the mesa road marked with Jal-Veesa's knot and are stacked by the stair down to the cellar. The quartermaster stores them and asks nothing; the fort has no Hist and its people go to Noota Nara's tree.
Three Sarpa raiders rob the chalk carts on the western road; the wall captain will not open the keep to strangers while his men are needed on the walls.
A gaoler of the Toh-Reel-Ka stands before the inner door and turns everyone away, the order's own people too. He carries no key.

facts.claim: The wall captain will open the keep to a Toh-Wo once the three Sarpa raiders on the western approach are dead; until then a Toh-Wo may only sleep in the barracks.
The stair down to the cellar starts in the quartermaster's store, behind an Adept lock; the quartermaster carries its key.
Jars of Hist sap marked with Jal-Veesa's knot are stacked by the cellar stair, though the fort has no Hist and its people go to Noota Nara's tree.
The gaoler, of the Toh-Reel-Ka, turns away everyone from the inner door, Toh-Wo or not, and carries no key; Never-Writes-Twice keeps it.
"They sleep, and they dream. That is all they do down there."
Moaning comes from behind the locked inner door, and no key in the fort opens it.

topics.label: What is Fort Chalkmoth?
topics.intent: Sakeeus-Wan answering the shared topic in his own words. Tells: an old Legion fort on the Chixathe Mesa, the high ground above Noota Nara; his garrison of the Archwardens takes a toll on the chalk carts and watches the Sarpa to the west; the old prison below the keep is the order's, not his. Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.

topics.label: Who are the Sarpa?
topics.intent: Sakeeus-Wan. Tells: raiders of the western mesa, Argonians who live by robbing the road; three of them sit on the western approach by a cart they robbed, out past the wall. Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.

topics.label: The three raiders on the western approach are dead.
topics.intent: Sakeeus-Wan. Checks: all three raiders dead. Tells: he gives the keep's key and a hundred gold; the stair to the old prison goes down from the quartermaster's store, and the quartermaster keeps that key himself; he warns that his leave covers the keep, not the store, and a man caught in another's store is a thief here like anywhere. Does: sets stage 20, whose start gives the key and the gold.

topics.label: Who are you?
topics.intent: Sakeeus-Wan. Tells: wall captain of Fort Chalkmoth for the Archwardens; his family has kept its keys since the Legion left; he trains archers on the wall. On the cellar he says only that the order keeps its own store down there and it is none of his business. Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.

topics.label: Who are you?
topics.intent: Theyne Indarys. Tells: the fort's quartermaster and smith, a Dunmer; he sells iron and steel and arrows; his store is his and stays locked. Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.

topics.label: Why are there jars of Hist sap in your store?
topics.intent: Theyne Indarys, once the player has seen or taken a jar. Tells: they come up the mesa road every season, tied with Jal-Veesa's knot, and go down the stair; the fort has no Hist and its people take their eggs and dead to Noota Nara's tree; he stores them and asks nothing, and advises the player to do the same. Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.

topics.label: (the gaoler speaks first) The cellar is closed.
topics.intent: Tsleel-Vaku, gaoler of the Toh-Reel-Ka, before the inner door. Tells: the cellar is closed to the player, Toh-Wo or not; nobody goes through this door; he carries no key; Never-Writes-Twice keeps it; go back up. Checks: nothing. Does: nothing (the objective completes).

state.notes: Fort Chalkmoth: killed the three Sarpa raiders, got the keep key and 100 gold from wall captain Sakeeus-Wan. Lifted the quartermaster Theyne Indarys store key and opened his store, but it holds nothing of note. The cellar door is in the fort yard and needs its own key, which the gaoler Tsleel-Vaku says Never-Writes-Twice keeps in Helstrom, so it cannot be picked. Tsleel-Vaku refuses entry; his only words were that they sleep and dream down there. My persuade and illusion attempts did not change the journal. Theyne says Hist sap jars tied with Jal-Veesa knot come up the mesa road each season and go down the cellar stair. The fort has no Hist and its people take eggs and dead to the Noota Nara tree. I still carry the Unbound recipe for the Seal. Next: get the cellar key from Never-Writes-Twice in Helstrom, who dismissed this fort earlier and so looks suspicious, or go to Bell Station for the tower. I never got a look at the cellar. The Collector Vanin is also digging ahead of us.

know_text: Grey Tooth quest done. The Grey Tooth cave niche was empty; a rubbing said the stone went to the Stormwidow, beached on Skeith Isle south-west shore. I took the Kings Marker Stone from its ballast crate (Unbound scouts were there; a wounded scout, Tah-Leesh, did not fight). I also took the Unbounds Recipe for the Seal, signed C.: grey caps and dried root ground into paste, numbs, pressed into the scar after the drawing. I still carry it. I gave the stone to Never-Writes-Twice in Helstrom and got 100 gold. She says the seven towers are the drowned spires off Lilmoth in Benthic Yobesh; the divers of Bell Station, an islet east of Lilmoth reached by boat from Lilmoth, know which tower is marked. Tah-Leesh said Cuts-the-Old-Knot tells the Toh-Reel-Ka to ask what moans in the cellar of Fort Chalkmoth (Archwarden fort, Chixathe Mesa above Noota Nara). Never-Writes-Twice dismissed it, which I find suspicious. Next: Bell Station for the tower, or Fort Chalkmoth first. The Collector Vanin is also digging ahead of us.
